title: Set up dbt for Fabric Data Warehouse
summary: A Microsoft Learn tutorial walking through installing the community-maintained dbt-fabric adapter, wiring a profiles.yml connection to a Fabric Warehouse, and running the standard dbt debug/seed/run/test cycle against it using the jaffle_shop sample project.
audience: Data engineers and analytics engineers who already use dbt (or are evaluating it) and want to target a Fabric Data Warehouse instead of, or alongside, another dbt-supported platform.
why_it_matters: dbt is a widely adopted external transformation framework, and Fabric's support for it is via a third-party-maintained adapter rather than a first-party Fabric feature. Engineers need to know exactly what that adapter does and does not translate cleanly into Fabric's T-SQL surface before committing a transformation layer to it.
takeaways: dbt targets Fabric Warehouse through the dbt-fabric PyPI adapter, not a built-in Fabric capability; switching platforms is largely a profiles.yml `type` change.
The adapter is installed and driven from outside Fabric (VS Code/CLI), requiring Python, the Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server, and a SQL analytics endpoint connection string.
Authentication is Microsoft Entra ID based, with Azure CLI recommended for interactive work and service principals recommended for automated/production runs.
Not all T-SQL operations dbt might issue are supported in Fabric Warehouse; the adapter works around this by favoring CTAS plus DROP/CREATE rather than full ALTER semantics.
Operationalizing dbt runs in production Fabric pipelines is documented separately as an Apache Airflow integration inside Fabric Data Factory, not as a native dbt orchestration feature.

claims.text: Fabric Data Warehouse is supported as a dbt target via the dbt-fabric adapter, a Python package published on PyPI and installed with `pip install dbt-fabric`, rather than through a Fabric-native dbt integration.

Setting up dbt against Fabric Warehouse requires Python 3.7+, the Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server, and an existing Fabric Warehouse (which can be created on trial capacity) before the adapter can connect.

A dbt project connects to Fabric Warehouse through a profiles.yml output block that sets `type: fabric`, the SQL analytics endpoint host, the database/schema names, an ODBC driver string, and an authentication mode.

Moving an existing dbt project between supported warehouse platforms (e.g., Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool and Fabric Warehouse) is a three-step process: install the target platform's adapter, change the `type` value in profiles.yml, and rebuild the project — no model rewrite is implied.

Fabric recommends Microsoft Entra ID authentication for dbt-fabric connections: interactive CLI-based authentication (via `az login`) for day-to-day development work, and service principal authentication for unattended/automated dbt runs.

The dbt-fabric adapter implements certain T-SQL operations dbt models rely on — including behaviors equivalent to ALTER TABLE ADD/ALTER/DROP COLUMN, MERGE, TRUNCATE, and sp_rename — by translating them into CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) plus DROP/CREATE sequences, because Fabric Data Warehouse's T-SQL surface does not support the same command set as SQL Server.

dbt projects targeting Fabric Warehouse are subject to Fabric Data Warehouse's general T-SQL command limitations and unsupported data types for tables; these are the same platform-wide constraints that apply outside of dbt, not adapter-specific restrictions.

Fabric documents operationalizing scheduled dbt runs by pairing dbt with Apache Airflow inside Fabric Data Factory, using Airflow's DAG-based scheduling and task orchestration to trigger dbt runs on a recurring basis, rather than via a native dbt scheduler in Fabric.

The standard dbt-fabric validation workflow after configuring profiles.yml is `dbt debug` (test connectivity), `dbt seed` (load sample/seed data), `dbt run` (execute models), and `dbt test` (validate data against tests), demonstrated end-to-end against Fabric Warehouse using the open-source jaffle_shop demo project.

The dbt-fabric adapter is maintained as an open-source project on GitHub under the microsoft org, where users are directed to file adapter-specific issues rather than through general Fabric support channels.
